units.text: INT. BARBERSHOP, SILVER GULCH - DAY
Striped pole.
Brass spittoon.
Through the window, a gallows is being quietly dismantled across the street.
JUDGE AMBROSE LITTLEFIELD, sixty, sits in the barber's chair under a white cloth.
SHERIFF NATHANIEL WREN, forties, stands at the door with his hat in his hands.
DOC SILAS FAIRWEATHER, a tall consumptive, sits by the stove.
ROSALIND MARCHAND, called ROSIE, thirty, the barber, strops a razor.
DEPUTY CALEB, nineteen, holds the broom.
Cut it short, Rosie.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: Not too short, Judge. You'll feel the draught.
units.name: ROSIE

units.text: He won't be out of doors much.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Nathaniel, I'll be out of doors a good deal. Don't you worry.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: You look better than you did in March.
units.name: DOC

units.text: I look like a man who sentenced the wrong brother.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: You sentenced the one the jury found.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Juries find what you set in front of them.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: Hold still.
units.name: ROSIE

units.text: Is the rope down yet?
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: Yes, sir. Half an hour ago.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: Good boy. Sweep the sawdust before the wind takes it.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: The mare's saddled at the livery. Provisions are in the left bag.
units.name: WREN

units.text: You've been thoughtful.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: Rosie packed the bread.
units.name: WREN

units.text: It's a day old.
units.name: ROSIE

units.text: Everything's a day old in this town.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: Where will you go?
units.name: DOC

units.text: South. There's a Judge in Albuquerque who owes me a sherry.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: You don't drink sherry.
units.name: ROSIE

units.text: No. But it's owed.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: Ambrose.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Yes, Nathaniel.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: I'll keep the bench warm.
units.name: WREN

units.text: You'll keep it clean. That's the harder thing.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: Rosie wipes the razor on her apron and sets it on the shelf.
That's the last of it.
units.name: ROSIE

units.text: Thank you, Rosalind. What do I owe you?
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: Two bits.
units.name: ROSIE

units.text: Two bits for the cut of a lifetime.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD

units.text: Three, if you stay for the shave.
units.name: ROSIE

units.text: No. No, I believe I'll go as I am.
units.name: LITTLEFIELD
